data.title: JavaScript
data.tagline: A programming language that makes a web page respond to actions and data
data.learningOutcome: You can explain how one click can request new data and update what a page shows.
data.description: When someone marks a task complete, browser JavaScript can send a request, receive the updated list, and change that row on the page. JavaScript can also run on a server through Node.js, which is a different environment with different responsibilities.

learning.assumes: You know a page button can be clicked.
learning.outcome: You can explain how one click can request new data and update what a page shows.

explanation.title: Handle the click and update the view
explanation.text: JavaScript runs the action prepared for that button, changes the relevant text or state, and the browser redraws that part of the screen.

explanation.title: Wait for server results and read console errors
explanation.text: It can request data over the network. If something goes wrong, the browser Console displays red errors (like TypeError). Copying the exact error to AI is much more effective than just saying 'the page is broken'.

explanation.title: Recognize basic syntax from AI
explanation.text: You don't need to memorize all syntax, but recognizing keywords like const/let (variables), function or => (actions), and if (conditions) helps you understand what AI is doing.

data.boundary: Browser JavaScript runs on the visitor’s device; Node.js server code runs elsewhere. Do not keep passwords or trusted permission checks only in browser code.

lessonPractice.title: A favorite count changes from 4 to 5 after clicking but returns to 4 after refresh. How should the issue be understood?

options.label: JavaScript updated the current view, but the save request and server result still need verification
options.feedback: Browser logic can change the view immediately, while refresh depends on whether the data was persisted.

options.label: The number changed, so saving succeeded and refresh should simply be blocked
options.feedback: A view update is only browser state and does not prove the server stored the favorite.

options.label: Put all favorite permission checks in the browser and let the server accept the result
options.feedback: Browser code can be modified, so real permissions and data rules require a controlled server check.

data.agentPrompt: Audit the favorite-button JavaScript: show saving, mark favorited only after success, and restore with retry on failure. Keep permissions and final data validation on the server, then refresh to verify persistence.
